# Letterboxd Films, Reviews, Lists & Member Activity Scraper

Turn public Letterboxd pages into clean, typed JSON. This actor reads film pages, review pages,
lists, browse pages, people filmographies, and public member pages exactly as a logged-out
visitor sees them. It needs no Letterboxd account, cookies, API key, or proxy configuration.

Use it to build film-metadata catalogues, review corpora, rating-distribution datasets, list
rankings, member diary exports, and person filmographies.

## Modes

| Mode | What it returns |
|---|---|
| **Films** | One record per film slug/URL: full metadata, cast, crew by role, themes, release calendar, similar films, external ids, optional stats and rating histogram. |
| **Search** | Letterboxd's own film search, as fast stubs or full film records. |
| **Member profile** | Display name, bio, avatar, member-since, film/list/follower stats, and favourite films. |
| **Watchlist** | A member's public watchlist, with position and total count. |
| **Watched films** | A member's public watched films with their personal rating and like flag. |
| **Diary** | A member's public diary for a year: watched date, rating, like, rewatch, review link. |
| **Member reviews** | A member's public film reviews. |
| **Member lists** | A member's public lists with film/like/comment counts. |
| **Lists** | One list's metadata, statistics, comments count, and every film in order; or the popular-lists index. |
| **Popular films** | This week/month/year/all-time rankings, optionally scoped to a genre. |
| **Browse** | Any Letterboxd `/films/...` page: genre, decade, year, language, country, theme, streaming service, rating/date sorts. |
| **Film reviews** | Reviews for one film, with five sort orders, exact half-star filtering, and optional full text. |
| **Filmographies** | Films by any of Letterboxd's crew roles, plus studio and country pages. |

The default run scrapes one film and returns one record. Every mode paginates automatically up to
`maxItems` (1–1000).

## Film fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `slug`, `url`, `id` | Letterboxd film slug, public URL, and slug used as id. |
| `title`, `year`, `originalTitle` | Title, release year, and original-language title when different. |
| `directors`, `cast`, `castMembers` | Director names; cast names; cast names with profile URLs and character names when Letterboxd publishes them. |
| `crew` | Object keyed by role (Director, Producers, Writers, Editor, Cinematography, Composer, Sound, …), each an array of `{name, url}`. |
| `genres`, `countries`, `productionCompanies` | Genre, country, and studio names. |
| `originalLanguages`, `languageCodes`, `primaryLanguage`, `spokenLanguages` | Languages as published by Letterboxd. |
| `runtimeMinutes`, `tagline`, `description` | Runtime, tagline, and synopsis. |
| `posterUrl`, `backdropUrl` | Poster and backdrop image URLs. |
| `averageRating`, `ratingsCount`, `reviewsCount` | Weighted average (0.5–5), rating count, review count. |
| `fansCount`, `fansCountText` | Fans count from the film page as a number and as published text (`202K fans` → `202000`). Exact below 1,000; abbreviated above. |
| `ratingHistogram`, `ratingPercentages` | Counts/percentages for the ten half-star buckets. |
| `watchedCount`, `listsCount`, `likesCount`, `top500Rank` | Member watched/list/like counts and Top 500 rank when ranked. |
| `alternativeTitles`, `themes` | Alternative titles and Letterboxd themes. |
| `releaseDates`, `releaseDate` | Release events by country/type/certification/note, and the earliest date. |
| `similarFilms` | Up to eight similar films (`slug`, `title`, `year`, `url`). |
| `imdbId`, `tmdbId`, `tmdbType`, `letterboxdId`, `filmId` | External and Letterboxd identifiers. |
| `whereToWatch`, `trailerUrl` | Optional (toggle): regional streaming/rent/buy/disc offers with price/currency, and the trailer URL. |

## Review fields

`filmSlug`, `filmTitle`, `filmYear`, `reviewerUsername`, `reviewerDisplayName`,
`reviewerAvatarUrl`, `rating`, `likedFilm`, `rewatch`, `reviewUrl`, `date`, `text`, `language`,
`hasSpoilers`, `commentsCount`, `likesCount`, `isTextTruncated`, `id`, `viewingId`. Long review
text is expanded when **Load full review text** is on.

## List, member, diary, and crew fields

- **List:** `owner`, `listSlug`, `url`, `id`, `title`, `description`, `ownerDisplayName`,
  `publishedAt`, `updatedAt`, `tags`, `listId`, `filmsCount`, `hours`, `directorsCount`,
  `countriesCount`, `languagesCount`, `commentsCount`, `likesCount`, `likesPageUrl`.
- **Member profile:** `username`, `url`, `displayName`, `bio`, `memberSince`, `avatarUrl`,
  `filmsLogged`, `filmsThisYear`, `listsCount`, `followingCount`, `followersCount`,
  `favoriteFilms`.
- **Diary:** `id`, `viewingId`, `diaryOwner`, `diaryYear`, `filmSlug`, `filmUrl`, `filmTitle`,
  `filmYear`, `watchedDate`, `rating`, `liked`, `rewatched`, `reviewUrl`.
- **Watched films/watchlist:** film fields plus `watchedBy` or `watchlistOwner`,
  `ownerRating`/`ownerLiked`, and `watchlistPosition`/`watchlistTotal`.
- **Crew member:** `crewType`, `slug`, `url`, `id`, `name`, `description`, `filmsCount`.
- **Browse/popular/filmography film rows:** `slug`, `title`, `year`, `averageRating`,
  `url`, plus `crewType`/`crewSlug`, `sourceList`, or list position where relevant. Browse and
  popular rows also carry `totalFilms`, the source query's own total before your filters
  (for example `79,828` for the horror genre).

Empty values are omitted at every depth. The dataset never contains `null`, `""`, `[]`, or `{}`.

## Examples

### One film with statistics

```json
{
  "mode": "film",
  "filmSlugs": ["parasite-2019", "https://letterboxd.com/film/dune-part-two/"],
  "includeStatistics": true,
  "maxItems": 2
}
```

### Film reviews, highest rated, full text

```json
{
  "mode": "filmReviews",
  "filmSlug": "parasite-2019",
  "reviewSort": "entry-rating",
  "reviewRating": "4.5",
  "reviewFullText": true,
  "maxItems": 50
}
```

### A member's diary and watched films

```json
{
  "mode": "userDiary",
  "username": "dave",
  "diaryYear": 2025,
  "maxItems": 100
}
```

```json
{
  "mode": "userFilms",
  "username": "dave",
  "userFilmRating": "4.5",
  "maxItems": 100
}
```

### A list and the popular-lists index

```json
{
  "mode": "lists",
  "listUrl": "https://letterboxd.com/official/list/letterboxds-top-500-films/",
  "maxItems": 200
}
```

```json
{
  "mode": "lists",
  "popularPeriod": "week",
  "maxItems": 25
}
```

### Browse and filmographies

```json
{
  "mode": "browse",
  "browseUrl": "https://letterboxd.com/films/genre/horror/",
  "maxItems": 100
}
```

```json
{
  "mode": "byCrew",
  "crewType": "cinematography",
  "crewSlug": "hong-kyung-pyo",
  "maxItems": 100
}
```

## Input reference

| Input | Used by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | all | One of the 13 modes. |
| `filmSlugs` | Films | Slugs or full URLs. |
| `filmSlug` | Reviews | Single film slug or URL. |
| `searchQuery` | Search | Autocomplete caps at 100 films. |
| `enrichSearchResults` | Search | Visit each result for full metadata. |
| `username` | all member modes | Handle or profile URL. |
| `listUrl` | Lists | Empty returns the popular-lists index. |
| `browseUrl` | Browse | Any `/films/...` page. |
| `popularPeriod` | Popular, Lists | week / month / year / all-time. |
| `crewType`, `crewSlug` | Filmographies | 24 roles + studio + country. |
| `genre` | Popular, film filters | 19 Letterboxd genres. |
| `minYear`/`maxYear`, `minRating`/`maxRating`, `minRuntime`/`maxRuntime`, `minRatingsCount` | films and listings | Filters; full data is fetched when needed. |
| `reviewSort`, `reviewRating`, `reviewFullText` | Reviews | Five sorts, exact half-star filter, optional full text. |
| `userFilmRating` | Watched films | Exact half-star filter. |
| `diaryYear` | Diary | Defaults to the current year. |
| `includeStatistics` | Films, Search, listings | Adds stats + histogram (two extra requests per film). |
| `includeAvailability` | Films and listings | Adds where-to-watch offers + trailer. |
| `maxItems` | all | 1–1000. |
| `proxy` | all | Optional. The actor works without it. |

## FAQ

**Do I need a Letterboxd account or API key?**
No. Every mode reads pages Letterboxd serves to logged-out visitors. The actor does not use
Letterboxd's official API.

**Why is the proxy field empty?**
Because it is not needed. The actor uses a browser-like TLS fingerprint and cookie refresh to read
public pages directly, and switches to a bundled headless Chromium when a network challenge
appears. If direct access is challenged repeatedly, the actor picks an Apify Proxy automatically;
no setup or extra input is needed. The optional proxy field only exists if you prefer to pin your
own Apify Proxy.

**Why does Search return at most 100 films?**
That is Letterboxd's autocomplete response cap, confirmed across 30 diverse queries and parameter
variants; no keyless surface returns more for one query. The full search page returns 20 films and
the anonymous public API returns 72 film items whose cursor does not advance. For a longer list,
use Films mode with explicit slugs, or Browse mode with a genre/decade/year page.

**How many reviews can I get for one film?**
Letterboxd serves 12 reviews per page and stops each sort order at 256 pages (3,072 reviews). Use
the exact half-star filter to reach other buckets, and raise `maxItems` to keep collecting.

**Are character names included for cast members?**
Yes. When Letterboxd publishes them, each `castMembers` row includes a `character` field beside
the actor name and profile URL. A few documentary or voice credits have no character; those rows
omit the field.

**Is a fans count available?**
Yes. Every film page publishes a fans count beside the ratings header, and the actor ships it as
`fansCount` (a number) and `fansCountText` (as shown, e.g. `202K fans`). Counts below 1,000 are
exact; above that Letterboxd abbreviates them. The separate fans page lists members but has no
total and stops at page 256 (6,400 fans), so an exact total for a very popular film is not
published anywhere.

**What is `totalFilms`?**
Browse and popular modes read the per-query total that Letterboxd prints on the browse page (for
example `There are 79,828 films` for the horror genre). It is the size of the source query before
the optional year/rating/runtime filters are applied, so it tells you how deep that browse page is.

**Does the actor localise titles?**
The public site has no locale UI: `?locale=`, an `Accept-Language` header, and locale cookies all
leave the English page unchanged. `/fr/film/...` returns 404; `/fr/` is a member profile named
`fr`, not a locale route. Letterboxd does publish original titles and a list of alternative
titles, which the actor includes.

**How current is the data?**
Every run reads Letterboxd live. Schedule the actor to track rating drift, new reviews, list
changes, or member activity.

**Is this affiliated with Letterboxd?**
No. This is an independent third-party tool that reads public pages. Letterboxd's terms restrict
automated data gathering; check them and use the actor only for lawful, respectful collection of
public reference data.

## Limitations

- 3,072 reviews per sort order (256 pages × 12). Use the rating filter to reach more.
- Search autocomplete returns at most 100 films per query; the full search page returns 20, and
  the anonymous public API's cursor does not advance. This cap is confirmed by an independent
  audit.
- No locale-specific UI: `?locale=`, `Accept-Language`, and locale cookies leave the English page
  unchanged; `/fr/film/…` is 404 (`/fr/` is a member profile named `fr`). Original and
  alternative titles are the available substitutes.
- Fans counts above 1,000 are abbreviated on the film page, and the fans page has no total and
  stops at 256 pages (6,400 fans), so an exact total for very popular films is not published.
- Private watchlists return HTTP 403 to logged-out visitors and produce a clear status message.
  Letterboxd has no private profiles; private diary entries are hidden by Letterboxd while the
  diary page itself remains public.
- Where-to-watch offers depend on the region Letterboxd/JustWatch assigns to the request IP.
- Some films genuinely lack a tagline, themes, release calendar, cast, character names, or rating;
  those fields are omitted for those records rather than filled with placeholders.
- A few Letterboxd pages (for example a country filmography or a list's likes page) can show a bot
  challenge to a plain scripted request; open the URL in a normal browser and it loads.
